qdc_qhc_relationship.summary: City Plan s1.6 (Table 1.6.1) expressly identifies which planning-scheme provisions are building assessment provisions: (a) ss32(c)/33 Building Act 'alternative provisions' to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 performance criteria 1 (road setbacks), 2 (side/rear boundary clearance) and 3 (site cover) - items 10, 11, 12; and (b) s32(b) BA / s6 Building Regulation 'qualitative statements and quantifiable standards' for QDC MP1.1/1.2 performance criteria 4 (height), 5 (privacy) and 8 (parking) - items 6, 7, 8. For a standard (>= 450 m2, non-small) lot the Dwelling house code contains NO setback or site cover provisions - only height (AO2/AO3, item 6), parking (AO4, item 8) and approved building envelope plan (AO7, items 6/10/11); its AO2 editor's note states side setbacks come from the QDC. So for standard lots, boundary clearance/site cover for houses and Class 10a come from the QDC/QHC unless a neighbourhood plan provision listed in Table 1.6.1 or the TBC design overlay applies. For small lots (< 450 m2 or rear lot < 600 m2) the Dwelling house (small lot) code front/side/rear setbacks, built-to-boundary walls, shared walls and site cover/impervious area are alternative provisions that replace QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 values. Council's referral-agency role (Table 1.6.2) covers non-compliance with these alternative provisions/qualitative statements and amenity-and-aesthetics referral (s1.7.4) in the listed zones. NO reference to the Queensland Housing Code (QHC) was found anywhere in City Plan v37.00/2026 (full-text search of all downloaded sections for 'Housing Code' returned nothing); Table 1.6.1 still cites 'QDC parts MP1.1 and MP1.2'. Council's own 'Rules for boundary setback' web page (COUNCIL_FACTSHEET) also still directs users to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 and states City Plan's small lot code prevails over the QDC. A secondary source (thegoodbuilder.com.au, SECONDARY_SOURCE_ONLY) states that the old provisions continue to apply to a council planning scheme until the earlier of an amendment stating how the Code applies or 1 September 2029 - this transitional rule must be verified against the QHC / Building Regulation transitional provisions.

quotes.text: - This planning scheme, through Part 5, regulates building work in accordance with sections 32 and 33 of the Building Act 1975.

Editor’s note—The Building Act 1975 permits planning schemes to: - regulate, for the Building Code of Australia (BCA) or the Queensland Development Code (QDC), matters prescribed under a regulation under the Building Act 1975 (section 32).These include variations to provisions contained in parts MP1.1, MP1.2 and MP1.3 of the QDC such as heights of buildings related to obstruction and overshadowing, siting and design of buildings to provide visual privacy and adequate sight lines, on-site parking and outdoor living spaces. It may also regulate other matters, such as designating land liable to flooding, designating land as bushfire prone areas and transport noise corridors; - deal with an aspect of, or matter related or incidental to building work prescribed under a regulation under section 32 of the Building Act 1975; - specify alternative boundary clearances and site cover provisions for Class 1 and 10 structures under section 33 of the Building Act 1975 Refer to Schedule 9 of the Regulation to determine assessable development, the type of assessment and any referrals applying to the building work.

rules.verbatim_text:
AO26.1
Development ensures that shared walls located on one or more side boundaries have a maximum length that:
- is 20m, or 60% of the length of the side boundary, whichever is lesser;
- does not exceed the length of an abutting approved or lawfully constructed shared wall of an adjoining dwelling; or
- complies with an approved development footprint plan for the site.
Refer to Figure m.
Note—Shared walls refer to adjoining walls that are built on each side of a common boundary. A High-density development easement is required to manage the shared wall with the adjacent lot.
Note—Length is the cumulative length of the wall on a side boundary, with each side measured separately. 
Note—Where demonstrating compliance with PO28/AO28.1 in the Subdivision code, compliance with this acceptable outcome must be noted on a development footprint plan. | AO26.2
Development ensures that shared walls have a maximum wall height that: 
- is 11.5m;
- does not exceed the extent of an approved or lawfully constructed shared wall of an adjoining dwelling; or
- complies with an approved development footprint plan for the site.
Refer to Figure m.
Note—Where demonstrating compliance with PO28/AO28.1 in the Subdivision code, compliance with this acceptable outcome must be noted on a development footprint plan. | AO26.3
Development locates a shared wall:
- on one side boundary; or
- on both side boundaries, only where the site has an average lot width of 9m or less and is not a corner lot; or
- in accordance with an approved development footprint plan for the site.
Note—Where demonstrating compliance with PO28/AO28.1 in the Subdivision code, compliance with this acceptable outcome must be noted on a development footprint plan. | AO26.4
Development ensures that a shared wall is:
- adjoining a shared wall on an adjoining lot;
- not located along a front or rear boundary;
- only located on one side boundary where a corner lot;
- constructed of pre-finished or low maintenance materials; or
- in accordance with an approved development footprint plan for the site.
Note—Where demonstrating compliance with PO28/AO28.1 in the Subdivision code, compliance with this acceptable outcome must be noted on a development footprint plan.
Editor's note—To ensure that a shared wall remains low maintenance, a development that incorporates a roof design with deep overhangs which falls to the front and/or rear boundaries (ie. away from the boundary with the shared wall) is effective at ensuring roof water shed is not directed to adjoining properties or spaces between shared walls. Roof design with overhangs, avoiding parapet facades with box gutter or concealed eaves gutter details will mitigate the impacts of overflow.

local_plan_mechanism.summary: Neighbourhood plans (Part 7, 80+ NP codes) vary outcomes in two ways: (1) Table 5.9.x tables can change the category of assessment for a dwelling house (e.g. Sherwood-Graceville Westside character precinct makes new dwelling houses code assessable); (2) NP code acceptable outcomes can vary setbacks/height/site cover. Only those NP provisions listed in Table 1.6.1 are building-assessment provisions (alternative provisions / qualitative statements) - e.g. Centenary suburbs, City west, Forest Lake, Fortitude Valley, Ithaca, Latrobe and Given Terraces, Moreton Island settlements, New Farm and Teneriffe Hill, Nathan-Salisbury-Moorooka, Newstead and Teneriffe waterfront, Nudgee Beach, Spring Hill, River gateway, Sandgate Road and West End-Woolloongabba PO1/AO1 (height, item 6); Forest Lake PO4/AO4.1, Sherwood-Graceville PO3/AO3.3 (item 10); Forest Lake PO4/AO4.1, New Farm and Teneriffe Hill PO3/AO3 and PO6/AO6, Sherwood-Graceville PO3/AO3.4-AO3.5 (item 11). Other NP numeric provisions (e.g. New Farm AO5 site cover 50%, Sherwood AO1.1 footprint 50%) are planning benchmarks only. The Dwelling house code itself notes: zone, precinct, NP or overlay outcomes prevail to the extent they vary the code.

open_questions: QHC transition: City Plan v37 Table 1.6.1 still refers to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2. Confirm under the QHC / Building Regulation 2021 transitional provisions how these alternative provisions map onto QHC Chapters 1 and 2 (and whether performance-criteria numbering P1-P9 is preserved). A secondary source says old provisions continue to apply to a scheme until an amending scheme or 1 Sept 2029 - not verified from primary text.

Standard (non-small) lots: Brisbane provides no setback/site-cover alternative provisions in the Dwelling house code, so QHC Chapter 2 values govern Class 10a siting unless an NP provision listed in Table 1.6.1 or TBC overlay AO1.2/AO2.1 applies. Each NP listed in Table 1.6.1 (15+ codes) should be extracted individually if those areas are in scope.
Table 1.6.1 item 9 references 'Bushfire overlay code PO21 and AO21.2' but the current Bushfire overlay code (8.2.5) only runs to PO20/AO20.2 - stale cross-reference.
Dwelling house (small lot) code AO5(c) garage 5.5m setback mentions 'garages' only; whether carports are captured needs certifier/Council interpretation (Section B AO22.2 uses 'covered car parking').
Small lot AO7 'average depth' is not defined in SC1.2 (only 'average width' is).

Small lot setbacks apply to 'development' with no Class 10a concessions (e.g. AO7 rear 3m/6m); confirm Council practice for sheds/carports in rear setback of small lots (likely concurrence referral under Table 1.6.2).

Swimming pools: City Plan contains no pool boundary setback provision; pools appear only in prescribed accepted development (Table 5.3.4.1) and as impervious area (small lot Section B AO20). Pool siting falls to QDC/QHC and pool safety laws.

Package W schedule (v37) text for Table 5.5.2 includes a note that 'All dwelling houses in the Low-medium density residential zone may become assessable development as the Dwelling house character overlay applies to all land within this zone' - this note was not present in the live ePlan Table 5.5.2 text retrieved; reconcile.
Dwelling house character overlay mapping extent per lot needs the overlay map (GIS) - not extracted.

HEIGHT GAP: neither the Dwelling house code (AO2 / AO3) nor Section A of the Dwelling house (small lot) code (AO3 / AO4) names the High density residential zone, so there is NO acceptable-outcome height for a dwelling house in HDR on a lot of 180 m2 or more. The '9.5 m' assumption for standard lots does not hold in HDR. For accepted-subject-to-requirements extensions there is no scheme height AO to meet (QDC/QHC height-dependent setbacks still apply); for assessable development only the performance outcomes (DH code PO2/PO3; small lot code PO3/PO4) could be used, and their zone scope is not stated. Section A AO2 (building envelope) refers to 'the acceptable outcome for maximum building height', which does not exist for HDR. Exceptions: lots < 180 m2 (Section B AO18: 11.5 m and 3 storeys, not zone-limited) and raising on a small lot under Table 5.3.4.1 row 4588 (9.5 m). Needs manual review / Council confirmation.

Existing brisbane.json records whose text applies in HDR (dh_parking_spaces, dh_secondary_dwelling_size, dh_building_envelope_plan, all sl_* except sl_max_height_low_density, sl_max_height_lmr_3_4_storey_mdr and sl_built_to_boundary_character_precinct, and all slb_*) have zones arrays that omit 'High density residential zone'. Recommend adding HDR to those arrays rather than duplicating records. NOT applicable in HDR: dh_max_height_low_density, dh_max_height_lmr_3_4_storey_mdr, dh_ridgeline_height, sl_max_height_low_density, sl_max_height_lmr_3_4_storey_mdr, sl_built_to_boundary_character_precinct, the AO6(c)(iv) limb of sl_side_zero_setback, tbc_* (TBC overlay not applied to dwelling houses in HDR; Pre-1911 overlay aside), np_* (the New Farm / Sherwood precincts named are not HDR).

Standard lots (>= 450 m2 and not a rear lot < 600 m2) in HDR: the Dwelling house code has no setback or site-cover AO, so Class 10a siting (setbacks, site cover) and pool siting fall to QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 (now QHC) through the Building Regulation 2021. The only scheme numbers are AO1.2 (secondary dwelling max 80 m2 GFA, within 20 m), AO4 (1 parking space) and AO7 (approved envelope).

Is a detached Class 10a outbuilding (shed/garage/carport) or a swimming pool on a non-small HDR lot 'Building work for an extension to a dwelling house' under Table 5.10.9? If not, it is not listed in Table 5.10.9 or Table 5.7.1 and is accepted development by default (s5.3.2 rule 21880), subject only to Building Regulation siting. On small lots, Table 5.3.4.1 row 4589 makes 1 shed (10 m2, 3 m), carports and pools prescribed accepted; other work outside the envelope falls back to Table 5.10.9 (small lot code). Needs Council/certifier confirmation.

Does the Dwelling house character overlay really cover every HDR lot? The Table 5.5.4 note says it 'applies to all land within this zone'; the overlay map (Schedule 2) was not checked lot by lot. If a lot were outside the overlay, Table 5.5.4 alone applies (MCU impact; building work accepted by default).

QHC transition: Table 1.6.1 still cites QDC MP1.1/MP1.2 (same issue as in brisbane.json). Dwelling house (small lot) code PO6/AO6 (incl. the HDR 15 m non-habitable length) is listed in Table 1.6.1 item 11 as an alternative provision; Dwelling house code PO7/AO7 in items 6, 10 and 11; PO4/AO4 in item 8.

Neighbourhood plans that include HDR land (e.g. inner-city NPs) may set dwelling-house siting numbers or change the category of assessment (section 5.9); none were extracted here. Table 1.6.1 item 6 lists NP codes (e.g. Spring Hill PO1/AO1 and PO7/AO7.2; West End-Woolloongabba PO1/AO1 and PO6/AO6.1-AO6.2; Fortitude Valley PO1/AO1.2) that may cover HDR land.
Heritage, Pre-1911 building, flood and other overlays can still raise the level of assessment in HDR (section 5.10); not extracted here.
